Diplomacy

/dih-PLOH-muh-see/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Diplomacy means the skill of managing relations between countries or people through careful, respectful discussion.

The two nations settled their fishing-rights dispute through quiet diplomacy instead of gunboats, and it took all of Grandma's diplomacy to settle the twins' daily battle over the window seat.

Worked Example

It took real diplomacy for the student council president to divide the activity budget without angering either the robotics team or the drama club.

She had to manage a touchy situation between two rival groups using sensitivity and careful words. That people-handling skill — keeping everyone talking and no one insulted — is diplomacy.

tact

Antonyms

tactlessness

tactlessness: careless, hurtful bluntness

belligerence

belligerence: hostile, aggressive behavior

How Strong Is It? — courtesy → diplomacy → statecraft

courtesy vs. diplomacy

courtesy vs. diplomacy: Courtesy is basic everyday politeness — saying please, thank you, and excuse me.

statecraft vs. diplomacy

statecraft vs. diplomacy: Statecraft is diplomacy at its grandest scale: the full art of steering a nation's affairs among rival powers.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — diplom

Root — diplom: a folded official paper (from Greek diploma, from diploos, 'double, folded over')

Suffix — -acy

Suffix — -acy: the practice or quality of

Put it together

Put it together: In ancient Greece, a diploma was an official paper folded double to keep its contents private. Diplomacy grew from the practice (-acy) of carrying and managing those folded state documents between governments — the paperwork of peace.

Use the root in a new word: diploma

Use the root in a new word: diploma: Her diploma — literally a 'folded paper' in ancient Greek — now hangs in a frame above her desk.

Word Choice

International affairs / everyday tact

At its grandest, diplomacy is the profession of managing relations between nations — embassies, envoys, and summit talks. But the word shrinks comfortably to personal scale: you can handle an awkward dinner-table conversation 'with diplomacy.' The related adjective form, diplomatic, appears in this unit's reading exercises.
